title: 2026-06-02-summit-signal-and-hiring-open-floor
summary: Monthly company summit: short metrics + one incident retro + updated hiring plan and open Q&A. Leadership focused on headcount pacing, reliability SLOs, and product priorities for H2. Action items assigned for benchmarking, hiring requisitions, and a follow-up all-hands on on-call rotations.
action_items: Aisha: Draft SLO proposal and schedule workshop (due 2026-06-09)
Maya: Finalize hiring prioritization doc and open requisitions for 6 roles (due 2026-06-05)
Jordan: Run capacity benchmark vs. public baseline and share spreadsheet (due 2026-06-12)
Leo: Update H2 roadmap doc with fallback strategies for Dedicated/Private (due 2026-06-08)
next_steps: Leadership will circulate the detailed incident timeline and post-mortem link
People ops to share updated hiring priority doc and calendar slot for role review
Schedule a follow-up all-hands focused on on-call and pager rotation policy
Engineering to run a 2-week cost vs latency experiment and report results
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 1:14
Attendees (selected): Evan West (CEO), Priya Rao (CTO), Aisha Green (VP Eng), Leo Martinez (VP Product), Maya Chen (Head of People), Jordan Kim (SRE) + ~120 staff on mute

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, sorry we're a bit behind schedule, we had a tiny calendar hiccup so welcome to the June Summit Signal and Hiring Open Floor. Quick housekeeping, recording is on, captions enabled. Evan wants to kick us off with a short state of the company.

[00:30] Evan: Thanks Maya. Hi team, quick high level — revenue continues to track ahead of plan, usage up about 32% q/q, runway extended by the efficiency work. Big thanks to infra and product. We're still seeing strong uptake for Dedicated among fintech customers which is great. That said, H2 we need to be disciplined on spend and prioritize hires that unblock product velocity.

[01:05] Priya: Just to add — from a tech side we shipped the continuous batching improvements last month, initial results show 12 to 18% token cost reduction on typical workloads, but there's variance per model. We'll share the segmented benchmarks later.

[01:35] Leo: On product, a handful of roadmap shifts — we're deferring the experimental multi-tenant quantization UI and instead shipping better rollout controls and model pinning for Dedicated customers. This should help with reliability and support case volume.

[02:10] Aisha: Before we move on, quick note on the incident last week — Jordan and the SRE team will run the full retro but the cliff notes: a cascade from an overloaded RPC queue, exacerbated by a misconfigured autoscaler policy and a stale kernel build on one pool. That produced elevated tail latency for roughly 27 minutes.

[02:52] Jordan: Yeah, sorry about that — we did a paged rotation, mitigations worked but a couple of things slipped -> the autoscaler threshold wasn't catching the unusual seq-lens; we also had a mismatch between the serving runtime version and the kernel flags. We've got a short term rollback and a rollout plan to backfill the patch. Full post-mortem coming.

[03:25] Evan: Appreciate the team response. I want to stress two things: one, customers generally didn't lose data, but some SLA targets were missed, and two, I want us to double down on runbooks and run the chaos drills more regularly.

[03:55] Staff (someone off mic): Is this linked to the KV cash problem we saw last month? (laughs)

[04:05] Jordan: Haha, kv cash — I think that was a separate cache invalidation bug but both incidents point to needing better telemetry at the request routing layer.

[04:28] Priya: Telemetry is being expanded — more per-route percentile metrics and request tagging so we can route based on sequence length and model variant. That helps scheduling and kernel selection.

[04:55] Maya: OK shifting to hiring — we've updated the hiring plan to reflect the current runway and priorities. We are approving 6 immediate roles: 2 infra engineers (SRE/serving), 2 product engineers (runtime), 1 security engineer, and 1 sales engineer focused on enterprise Dedicated deals.

[05:25] Maya: Open question for leadership — do we want to reallocate the remaining headcount from marketing to product, or keep some buffer?

[05:40] Evan: I'll start — lean into product and infra. The engine of our business is reliable inference and developer experience, we need to invest where it improves unit economics. Marketing is important but we can run lean experiments.

[06:05] Leo: Agreed, but let's be careful about sales coverage for Dedicated — losing motions there means missing bigger deals. The SE/Sales engineer hire is actually critical to close the pipeline.

[06:30] Aisha: I'll note that ops overhead is high with current oncall. Hiring infra SREs helps with rotating load and implementing better autoscaler policies.

[06:48] Jordan: Also, we should consider moving some Dedicated capacity to an alternate region for DR so we can failover without customer impact. That's a longer ops lift but worth prioritizing.

[07:10] Priya: Quick product note — customers keep asking about private deployment options with stronger KMS integrations and HSM. We're seeing SAML/SSO and audit logs as top asks for regulated accounts. That's pushing some roadmap items earlier.

[07:40] Evan: We should prioritize compliance primitives (SOC2 evidence, audit logs ingestion to customer SIEM) for enterprise motion. Maya, let's sync with legal next week.

[08:01] Maya: Will do.

[08:10] Audience question (Liam): Are we going to increase salaries or offer hiring bonuses?

[08:18] Maya: Short answer: compensation is being reviewed alongside the hiring plan. We have a merit cycle planned in July — more details soon. For now we are focusing on filling critical roles and reducing time-to-offer.

[08:40] Audience question (Pri): Can we get more context on the incident—why did kernel mismatch slip through?

[08:50] Jordan: It was partly human error in the release pipeline: a stale artifact was promoted because the tag we rely on was transient. We're adding artifact immutability checks and will include a verification step in CD.

[09:15] Priya: Also adding automated integration tests that run a small synthetic workload that mirrors production seq-length distribution; this should surface mismatches earlier.

[09:40] Evan: Switching gears — metrics. Net new ARR is up 11% this quarter, but churn ticked up by a couple of points for smaller customers who had cost-sensitive workloads. Our Optimize toolkit recommendations are helping some, but we need more automated guidance in the console so teams can self-serve cost/perf tradeoffs.

[10:10] Leo: We're going to prototype a "Cost Coach" in the Console: suggestions for batching, recommended quantization profiles and expected unit-cost impact. Early UX mocks will be shared in the product channel.

[10:37] Staff (quiet): Will that surface per-route per-model SLOs?

[10:43] Leo: Yes, the idea is to tie recommendations to route-level SLOs and guardrails so users can accept tradeoffs with confidence.

[11:05] Evan: Quick ask — let's avoid feature creep; the MVP should be suggestions + one-click application for caching and batching configs.

[11:20] Aisha: On reliability work: we'll pilot a regional fallback policy for Dedicated where requests can be routed to a compatible model variant in a different region if capacity is constrained. Need to test the latency impact though.

[11:45] Jordan: We'll run synthetic latency experiments and surface the delta. That goes into the benchmark doc.

[12:05] Audience (Sam): What's the plan for open-source engagement? We used to do more benchmarks and blog posts.

[12:15] Evan: We are scaling content but focusing on high-impact benchmarks that show production economics — latency/cost vs competing runtimes. We'll publish two benchmark posts this quarter.

[12:35] Priya: Also planning a small community workshop on quantization effects with invited contributors.

[12:50] Maya: OK, quick lightning Q&A — please drop questions in the Q&A feed. We'll call on a few.

[13:05] Audience (Elena): On the hiring list, can product do an internal slow-roll to promote from within?

[13:12] Leo: We always look internally first; there are candidates we're talking to internally for two of the product engineer spots. But timeline matters for infra roles.

[13:30] Audience (Marco): Can we get transparency on how priorities are set?

[13:38] Evan: We'll publish a short doc that maps objectives to top projects for H2 and share the prioritization rubric. Expect that by end of week.

[13:55] Employee (background): Applause — thanks leadership.

[14:05] Maya: We're at about 14 minutes into content — I'm going to speed through the remaining items: people ops updates (open comp reviews, parental leave reminders), product rituals (we're adjusting sprint length to 2 weeks), and an upcoming company offsite in September.

[14:30] Maya: Offsite will be in Lisbon, planning committee will send a survey for dates and dietary restrictions.

[14:50] Audience (Jo): Any change to the remote work policy?

[14:58] Evan: Minor adjustments — we'll keep core collaboration days and the rest flexible. People ops will share specifics.

[15:18] Priya: Back to technical — small note about Private: customers asked for HSM + on-prem connector. Engineering will scope a private pilot for Q3; it's non-trivial but doable.

[15:40] Jordan: On SRE staffing — we'll trial 24/7 rotation for 6 weeks with one extra hire covering overlap windows. We're hoping that reduces fatigue while we hire.

[16:05] Audience (quiet): How will this affect weekends?

[16:12] Aisha: The plan is to limit weekend pagers by adding automated runbooks and extra coverage, but we might still have an on-call. We'll share the rota.

[16:30] Evan: Final thing — I asked for three signals leadership should watch closely: 1) SLO burn rate, 2) unit cost per 1k tokens, 3) Dedicated conversion velocity. We'll track these on the weekly dashboard.

[16:58] Maya: Quick recap of next steps — hiring doc, incident post-mortem, SLO workshop, benchmarks. Any objections? Silence = thumbs up.

[17:15] Audience: (multiple mics, applause)

[17:25] Evan: Thanks everyone. We know this was dense — we'll post slides and notes. New hires, keep an eye on careers. Let's keep building.

[17:40] Maya: Meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: A short follow-up Slack thread with links to the hiring doc, the incident post-mortem (draft), and the benchmark ticket was shared within 30 minutes. Some caption errors in the transcript where "KV cache" is transcribed as "K V cash" and a few proper nouns were fuzzy.
